newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: INTERVIEW-Irish Life hopes to end sales row.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Irish Life hopes to end sales row.

text.p: Irish Life Plc said on Thursday that it was hopeful a dispute with its field sales force would be resolved soon and progress resumed on its sales and customer service agendas.
The company suspended most of its field force in February after failing to solve a 15-month old dispute over new work practices. Staff vote today on a new set of proposals.
"We await with interest. We hope to resolve the dispute as soon as possible," chief financial officer Stephen Shone told Reuters.
Earlier, the life assurance and investment group announced total profits after tax of 97.4 million Irish pounds in 1996 against 95.0 million a year earlier.
"We are extremely pleased. Operating profits are up, new business is up," Shone said.
Operating profit increased by nine percent to 93 million Irish pounds while new business rose by 42 percent to 11.8 million with sales in Ireland up 11 percent at 71.4 million.
But Shone said the dispute with the field sales force had a depressing effect on sales although he said it was difficult, if not impossible, to quantify the effect.
"Without that, you would have had a much better increase but given the circumstances we are very pleased with the numbers."
Irish Life said it looked forward to continued progress in 1997 and Shone said sales figures for the first two months of this year were encouraging.
"The U.S. is coming back more in line with the second half of 1996 and all the other areas are quite positive.

"Obviously again we have a depressing effect because of the PFA (personal financial adviser) dispute. There is no doubt about that but that is only a proportion of our business. We also have our corporate business and brokerage business," he said.
The group, which hopes to complete its $163 million purchase of Illinois-based Guarantee Reserve Life Assurance Company on Friday, said it remains on the lookout for further acquisitions.

"There is nothing definite at the moment but we continue to look for potential acquisitions," Shone said. "The area we are interested in is the U.S. although obviously we have to digest Guarantee Reserve first before we move on."
Irish Life also remains in the market for acquisitions closer to home.
"We are interested in the UK and we are interested in Ireland but obviously the consolidation of the markets in Ireland hasn't taken off so the opportunities are somewhat less," Shone said.
